primitives.name: Conditional Outcome Entropy
primitives.verbatim_quote: - Bias identification: Shannon entropy H(s) = -Σ_t p(o=t|s) log2(p(o=t|s)); low entropy = strongly biased spread (one side wins ATS far more often than the other).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'H(s)': 'dimensionless entropy', 'p(o=t|s)': 'probability of outcome t given spread s'}
primitives.assumptions: ['Outcome distribution is discrete and known', 'Spread s is fixed and deterministic', 'Low entropy implies predictable bias']
primitives.breakdown_regime: When p(o=t|s) approaches 0 or 1, entropy approaches zero

primitives.name: Kernel Density Estimation of Outcomes
primitives.verbatim_quote: Method / model - Estimate p(o|s): kernel density estimation (width = 4) over quantized outcomes -40..+40 per valid spread; then p(o=h|s) = ∫_{-∞}^{s} p(o|s)ds = Σ_{min s_a}^{s} p(o|s_a); p(o=v|s) = 1 - p(o=h|s).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'p(o|s)': 'conditional probability of outcome o given spread s', 'K': 'kernel function', 'h': 'bandwidth (4)', 'o_i': 'quantized outcome'}
primitives.assumptions: ['Quantized outcomes span ±40', 'Kernel width is fixed at 4', 'Outcomes are independent and identically distributed']
primitives.breakdown_regime: When sample size n is insufficient or bandwidth h too narrow

layer2.mapping: KDE provides smoothed empirical distribution for entropy computation

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that oddsmakers' spreads encode implicit biases detectable through conditional outcome entropy. By applying kernel density estimation to quantized outcomes around each spread, we derive p(o|s), enabling calculation of H(s). Low entropy suggests predictable bias—e.g., one team consistently wins ATS. The Min-Entropy primitive selects the single spread with lowest H(s), assuming this reflects true oddsmaker bias rather than noise. This contrasts with Max-Probability which uses all spreads, and Random-Guess which ignores structure. The failure mode arises when entropy thresholds are visually set without statistical validation, or when small-sample effects dominate. The method assumes that the final spread encodes all relevant game information, ignoring line movement and vigorish. Temporal consistency must be verified via walk-forward testing across seasons.
